event: "Granny Hua, Tie Bo and I have come to request your poison."
"To be used against the boar that has been foraging Zhao Jun's field."
"It may be too advanced to be effective."
"But if it is not, we are seeking any preparations that reduce the risk of further loss of life."
"We believe this to be the same boar that took Tie Bo's brother, and it has only grown stronger."
"If you have any additional counsel for us in this matter, we would be grateful for it."
Granny Hua listens to all of it without a word, her eyes never leaving Nala's face.
When it is done she grunts. "Plainly asked. That's more than I get from most."
She glances at Tie Bo. "Your brother's boar. I thought it might come to that."
Tie Bo says nothing, but his jaw tightens.
"I'll answer you," Granny Hua says to Nala. "But I don't deal with anyone I haven't looked at."
She lifts the latch and swings the gate open, and steps back into her yard, into the full sun.
The garden is rows of green: feathery leaves, grey-green leaves, tall stalks, some flowering blue.
She stops in the middle of it where the light is strongest, and turns to face Nala.
She holds out both her hands, palms up. They are brown and knotted, the nails rimmed green.
"Come here into the sun, spirit. Put your hands in mine. Both of them. Open."
